history.dynasty: Katyuri and Chand dynasties (Katyuri-era construction and restoration; Chand patronage)
history.period: 7th-13th century CE (sources vary between 7th-12th and 9th-13th - verify)
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the temple complex is at JAGESHWAR DHAM, ~35-37 km from Almora town, not in Almora itself; documented with the corrected location. One of India's largest assemblies of ancient stone temples (124-125 shrines), built over five centuries in Nagara style with Katyuri-characteristic craftsmanship, at 1,870 m on the banks of the Jataganga in a dense deodar forest. The principal shrine worships Shiva in the unusual form of Bal Jageshwar (Child Shiva). Locals claim it as the Nagesh Jyotirlinga, though it is not on the traditionally accepted list of twelve Jyotirlingas. The Mahamrityunjaya linga has a distinctive eye-shaped aperture. A protected monument under the Archaeological Survey of India, with an ASI site museum at the complex; it stood on an ancient trade route to Kailash Mansarovar.

name: Jageshwar Temple
town: Jageshwar, Almora district (CSV town 'Almora' is imprecise - the complex is ~37 km from Almora town)
town_description: Jageshwar is a small pilgrimage village in a deodar-forest valley on the Jataganga stream, ~37 km from Almora town. The temple complex stretches about 3.5 km along the river and includes the Dandeshwar and Kubera temple clusters; the quiet, mist-laden valley is a noted centre for meditation and nature walks.

travel.airport: Pantnagar Airport, the nearest airport (~150 km from Jageshwar per eUttaranchal/Outlook Traveller; one source says ~127 km from Almora - verify); road journey onward
travel.railway: Kathgodam railway station, the nearest major railhead (~125 km from Jageshwar; ~116 km per another source - verify), then road via Almora
travel.road: Jageshwar Dham is ~35-37 km from Almora by a scenic hill road, reachable by taxi or local bus; entry to the complex is free and the ASI museum is open 10:00 AM-4:00 PM

visitor_information.best_time: March to June and September to November (pleasant weather); the site is visited year-round and the monsoon festival draws crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict and vary by season: YatraDham gives 4:30 AM-7:30 PM (summer) / 5:00 AM-6:00 PM (winter); others cite 4:00 AM-6:00 PM or 6:00 AM-8:00 PM - confirm locally on arrival
